text: That history of recurrent biliary colic three years ago is very concerning for a stone obstructing the common bile duct. Have you noticed any lumps in your abdomen or back, and do you have a history of gallstones or pancreatitis? Additionally, have you had any recent fevers or chills?

text: I see; given your age, significant weight loss, and painless jaundice, I am particularly concerned about pancreatic cancer versus a biliary stone. Have you noticed any pain radiating to your back, and do you have any known gallstones or a history of pancreatitis?

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Choledocholithiasis (Common Bile Duct Stone) causing obstructive jaundice. The ultrasound findings of a cystic mass with bile duct dilation, combined with normal liver enzymes (AST/ALT) and negative tumor markers, strongly support a stone rather than pancreatic cancer. Do you recall any sudden relief of symptoms or passage of a stone in the stool recently?
